title: Response Models and Status Codes
learning_objectives: Separate input and output models so secrets never leave the API
Set success status codes such as 201 and 204
Return lists of models and handle conflicts with 409
Store a password hash instead of the password
hints: Add `response_model=UserOut, status_code=201` to the POST decorator and store `password_hash` instead of `password`.
Keep a counter (e.g. `state = {"next_id": 1}`) so deleted ids are not reused; check for an existing username first.
`@app.delete("/users/{user_id}", status_code=204)` and return `None`; `response_model=list[UserOut]` for the list.

failure_feedback.advice: Use `response_model=UserOut` and `status_code=201`, and never store the raw password.
Add the username pattern and length limits, the email pattern and an 8-character password minimum.
Check for an existing username before creating and raise HTTPException(409).
Use `response_model=list[UserOut]` for the list and return 404 for unknown ids.
Declare `status_code=204`, return None, and keep a separate id counter.
